title: The unslanderable raising of Lazarus
english: Let us bring the evangelist John into our midst again, for it is good to contemplate the firstfruits of the resurrection. You heard him say just now: "Six days before the Passover, Jesus came to Bethany, where Lazarus was, whom he had raised from the dead" (John 11:1). Did you see the firstfruits of the resurrection prefigured in Lazarus, which the faithful crowd recognized? The crowds recognized it, and the chief priests reviled the wonder-working, turning it into envy. They truly envied the resurrection of Lazarus, because after his resurrection, which you heard about, they plotted to kill him. Did you see the excess of envy? The one whom the Lord raised, they resolved to kill, not realizing that even if they killed him, it would again be easy for the Lord to raise his friend. They plotted to kill Lazarus. Nothing stung the Jews as much as the resurrection of Lazarus. This miracle alone they could not slander. They slandered the healing of the man born blind, saying, "This is he; no, it is not he; it is someone like him" (John 9:9). They slandered the raising of Jairus's daughter, saying that she had merely collapsed and had not been handed over to complete death. They slandered the resurrection of the widow's only son, saying that he had feigned death and had not been swallowed up by the tyranny of death. They slandered the withered fig tree, saying that it had been stripped by birds and not withered by the Lord's word. They slandered the changing of water into wine, saying that the dinner guests were already drunk and did not recognize the jest. Only the resurrection of Lazarus they could not slander. They knew Lazarus; the man was well known. They had followed the funeral procession, they had seen the tomb being sealed, they had consoled Martha and Mary, the sisters of Lazarus, according to custom, as at a funeral meal for the dead. They knew that he had lain in the tomb for exactly four days, and that he was a corpse four days dead, completely disjointed, his flesh wasted away, his bones loosened from their sockets, his sinews torn apart, his inward parts scattered, his belly dissolved. Knowing all this, when they suddenly saw the resurrection of Lazarus whole and complete, as from a lathe, gleaming with renewed life, they were thrown into confusion. They nearly fainted, finding no words of pretext for how they might slander the resurrection of Lazarus, since the Lord's strategy had arranged this. What does it mean that the Lord's strategy had arranged this? Listen briefly.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Amphilochius opens his homily by calling the congregation to look again at John's account of Lazarus, the firstfruits of the resurrection, and shows how the Jewish leaders could slander every other miracle but not this one.
